question: to the Commission Michele Picaro (ECR) Subject:

Transparent goby fishing is a traditional and seasonal endeavour that is particularly important to the economy of the Gulf of Manfredonia. According to reports, the scientists tasked with reviewing the proposed transparent goby management plan hold that the new scheme is an improvement over current arrangements, though they have also requested that DG MARE carry out further assessments. The failure to renew the management plan would be a further blow to jobs in the area and the local economy, and would have a direct bearing on the livelihoods of more than 120 fishers and on the future of around 60 vessels and a number of related businesses. In the light of the new data gathered by Italian researchers, including as regards fishing methods, and given the seasonal nature of transparent goby fishing, I ask the Commission: 1.
Will its assessment also take into account the important socio-economic role that transparent goby fishing plays for Manfredonia’s community and maritime economy?
What additional technical conditions or management measures does the management plan for 2025-2028 need to include in order to ensure that it is renewed?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.9.2026) The Commission is aware of the socio-economic importance of the transparent goby fishery for Manfredonia’s community and maritime economy. However, the Commission may grant a derogation from the prohibition to use towed gears set out in Article 13(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1967/2006 only if a number of the conditions set out in Article 13(5) and (9) are fulfilled. Based on the latest Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries (STECF) scientific evaluation1 of 2025, the Commission considers it necessary that a revised management plan addresses the concerns of STECF communicated through previous evaluations. The ongoing experimental fishery, notified by Italy and aimed at collecting more information, could help address the outstanding technical points raised by STECF. In addition, the revised management plan should provide sufficient monitoring, control and surveillance to ensure that the fishing operations concerned are conducted exclusively with boat seines, as defined in Article 2.1(ii) of Regulation (EC) No 1967/2006. The Commission may ask STECF to carry out a further evaluation of an updated management plan containing the main missing elements and management measures identified above.
